headline: Kept West End Farm Trail open pending mitigation talks, and recommended approval of a conditional use permit for 7 Rectory Rd.
summary: The land donation off Stickney Hill was accepted. Possible mitigation for the West End Farm Trail, such as fencing, will be discussed next month, and staff will look into fence and buffer options.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda with changes to the minutes; all in favor.
Approved reading into the record letters received during the public hearing, and not reopening the hearing for letters received later.
Voted to maintain the West End Farm Trail open and continue discussion of potential mitigation next month, with Member Porter abstaining.
Accepted the land donation off Stickney Hill with gratitude; all in favor.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve conditional use permit (2026-091) for 7 Rectory Rd as submitted, with no Commission concerns; all in favor.
Approved sealing the non-public meeting minutes, by roll call vote of 5 in favor and 0 opposed.

decision_evidence.quote: Alternate Member Owers moved, Member Coen seconded, to approve the consent agenda with the changes to the minutes. All in favor. The motion passed.

Member Lesser moved, Member Chorman seconded, to approve any letter that came in during the public hearing in the meeting to be read into the record and to not open the public hearing to read any letter(s) that came in after the meeting. All in favor. The motion passed.

Member Lesser moved, Member Coen seconded, to maintain the West End Farm Trail open and continue the discussion for potential mitigation next month and to engage with the Marro’s. All in favor. Member Porter abstained. The motion passed.
Member Chormann moved, Member Coen seconded, to accept the land donation with gratitude. All in favor. The motion passed.
Vice-Chair Lewis moved, Member Porter seconded, to recommend the Planning Board approve the conditional use permit as submitted and the Commission has no concerns. All in favor. The motion passed.

the Conservation Commission made a motion at 9:17 p.m. to seal the non-public meeting minutes due to Render the proposed action ineffective; or by roll call vote 5 in favor (Chormann, Coen, Lesser, Porter and Tardiff) to 0 opposed. The motion passed unanimously.

CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
1 
 
Attendees:      Chair Kristine Tardiff, Vice-Chair Jeff Lewis, Kevin Porter, Alternate Jim 
Owers, Rick Chormann, Mark Coen, Councilor Michele Horne, and Tracey 
Lesser  
 
Absent:  Katherine Healy and Alternate Member Bruce Currie  
 
Staff:   Kearsten O’Brien, Senior Planner 
  Alec Bass, Assistant City Planner – Community Planning 
  Krista Tremblay, Administrative Technician III 
     
Public:  Jessica Jacobson (2 Home Ave, Concord)  
 Jeff Litchfield (9 Columbia Ave, Concord) 
  
  
  
1. Call to Order 
The meeting was called to order by Chair Tardiff at 7:01 p.m.  
 
2. Consent Agenda: 
a. Minutes – Approve meeting minutes from meeting on October 14, 2026 
b. Forestry Report 
c. Local River Advisory Committees 
d. New Hampshire Department of Environmental Services 
Member Porter asked for the Forestry report to be pulled out of the consent agenda for there to be 
discussion on the topic.  
 
Ms. O’Brien asked if the Commission would like to have Mr. Klemarczyk to attend the meeting for 
discussion.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated if there are items from the forestry report to have discussion.  
 
Ms. O’Brien stated she can have a discussion with Mr. Klemarczyk to attend the Conservation 
Commission if there are items for discussion. Ms. O’Brien suggested if there was no discussion to be had 
on the Forestry report it could continue to be on the consent agenda and if a member would like to have it 
pulled from consent to notify Ms. O’Brien no later than noon on the day of the meeting. However, if the 
Commission would like for Mr. Klemarczyk to attend the meeting to provide advance notice for her to 
notify Mr. Klemarczyk.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated that works and do not need Mr. Klemarczyk every month.  
 
Alternate Member Owers has a change to the minutes on page 6 under the testimony of Shawn Reese the 
last sentence says should not exceed to the land owner and the word should be accede.
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
2 
 
Alternate Member Owers moved, Member Coen seconded, to approve the consent agenda with the 
changes to the minutes. All in favor. The motion passed. 
 
3. Decision regarding WEFT trail located at 74 Currier Rd. 
Chair Tardiff stated the Commission officially closed the public hearing at the end of the October 
meeting. There was discussion over the last two months. There will be no public testimony tonight. 
Chair Tardiff noted there was written testimony after the public hearing that did not make it into the 
record. Chair Tardiff noted the testimony is similar to what the Commission had already heard. Chair 
Tardiff asked the Commission if they would like the testimony to be added to the record.   
 
Ms. O’Brien stated there was on that came in after the fact and two received during the public 
hearing.   
 
Alternate Member Owers recommend not reading letters if they were received after the meeting and if 
they were received during the meeting to read into the record. 
  
Member Lesser moved, Member Chorman seconded, to approve any letter that came in during the 
public hearing in the meeting to be read into the record and to not open the public hearing to read any 
letter(s) that came in after the meeting. All in favor. The motion passed. 
 
Ms. O’Brien read the letter received during the public hearing last month that will be attached to the 
end of the meeting minutes. (need to add to the end of the meeting minutes) 
 
Chair Tardiff stated there was a photo received from the Marro’s that has been circulated to the 
Commission. Chair Tardiff noted for the Commission tonight they are to have a discussion on the 
West End Farm Trail and the potential discontinuance based on testimony. Chair Tardiff stated her 
and Vice-Chair Lewis went and met with the Marro’s to have a discussion on the trail. Chair Tardiff 
noted that Councilor Brown was also there at the invitation of the Marro’s. Chair Tardiff made it clear 
that they were not there to discuss the subject of tonight deliberation. There was conversation about 
mitigation issues that were raised at the public hearing.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis noted it was on October 28, 2026. 
 
Member Coen asked if there is a date on the photograph when it was taken.  
 
Ms. O’Brien stated there is no date stamped on the photo however, it was sent to her email on 
October 14, 2026. 
 
Member Coen noted in the photo there are trees cut and asked who was the one that cut the trees.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated they do not know that from the angle of the picture.  
 
Councilor Horne noted the Commission is not discussing the parking lot.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated the public notice for this meeting was only for discussion on the potential 
discontinuance of this portion of the West End Farm Trail. Chair Tardiff opened the discussion with 
the Commission.
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
3 
 
 
Alternate Member Owers stated he approached by the land owner in 2006 about the purchase of the 
property. Alternate Member Owers noted there are documents attached to the agenda. Alternate 
Member Owers noted the parcel is 85 acres with 218 feet of frontage on Currier Rd. Alternate 
Member Owers explained the plan was approved in 1999 and was recorded at the Merrimack County 
Registry of Deeds in 2000. The trail is shown on the plan and existed in 1999. Alternate Member 
Owers stated they purchased lot 2E. The trail on the plan is described as a 12-foot-wide right of way. 
There was also a well-used snow mobile trail at the time in corridor 11. Alternate Member Owers 
there was testimony at the meeting about the snow mobile trails. The prior owners of the lot did not 
care of the public used the trail and it was popular with the public. Alternate Member Owers noted the 
city acquired an easement with Diamond Hill and then Rossview Farm in 2007. This provided a way 
between the two parcels. Alternate Member Owers noted there was a report to the mayor and City 
Council and it is described as a critical trail and link to two adjacent protected properties. That is 
referring to the Rossview and Diamond Hill properties. The Commission agreed to pay $250,000 for 
the conservation fund in a unanimous vote. The matter went to City Council in 2008 and people 
testified how important the trail is to their snow mobile corridor. Alternate Member Owers stated the 
council vote passed unanimously in 2008 to purchase the property. However, the property went into 
foreclosure and there was a delay for two years. Alternate Member Owers noted in the documents 
there is a quick claim deed from the bank that foreclosed on the property in February of 2010. 
Alternate Member Owers stated the Conservation Commission has fee title to the land that was 
purchased from Concord funds and there are no easements on the land or restrictions on the deed. 
This is a permissible use of the property and the abutters should not interfere with the public right to 
use this property. Alternate Member Owers noted there was testimony about speakers on tree paying 
music, fallen trees, harassment on the trail, altering the gate, political signage and people not using 
the trail. Alternate Member Owers noted the abutter contended part of the trail was encroaching on 
his property. In 2021 the boundary line between lot 2D (76 Currier Rd) and 2E (74 Currier Rd) was 
resurveyed and as a result the trail was moved from the northeast corner. Alternate Member Owers 
noted when the surveyor was out there it was found that part of the shooting range was on city 
property, there was a speaker mounted to a tree on city property and a couple signs on city property. 
This was not a permissible use. Alternate Member Owers went through the trail criteria put out by the 
Trail Subcommittee and it provides a critical access for other trails. Alternate Member Owers noted 
there are bikes allowed on this trail and they are not permitted on the Rossview easement. Alternate 
Member Owers noted another criteria is does the trail have strong community support to keep the trail 
open and there was public testimony showing support of keeping this trail. Alternate Member Owers 
would like to keep the trail open for the public as it is now.  
 
Member Coen is concerned about the driving range location and what direction it faces. Could there 
be potential for harm to the public.  
 
Member Porter stated it is parallel to the trail and they are shooting north.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis asked if that is a reason why the trail should be closed.  
 
Member Coen noted the testimony he heard there was nothing compelling to close the trail and 
suggested to leave the trail open.
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
4 
 
Councilor Horne suggested to use the established criteria for trail closure and there are ten points to 
follow and suggested to follow the criteria.   
 
Member Porter stated when the Trails Subcommittee made their recommendation there was some 
language about mitigation. Member Porter stressed concern about making a decision without 
discussing the mitigation efforts.  
  
Chair Tardiff is limiting the discussion is the public notice stated there was a question on the 
discontinuance of the trail as part of the public hearing. Chair Tardiff noted any motion or decision 
can be put on the agenda for next month for further discussion.  
  
Vice-Chair Lewis would support a motion to keep the trail open. Vice-Chair Lewis feels strongly 
there should be mitigation on the trail as a part of that and if that is not to be discussed then the 
decision should be postponed. Vice-Chair Lewis stated for the benefit of the Marro’s prior to 2021 
when the survey was done the Marro’s came to the Conservation Commission regarding parking and 
trail access. Vice-Chair Lewis stated they bought the property in 2003 and built house in 2003-2004. 
Vice-Chair Lewis noted the trail at the time was a snow mobile trail. Vice-Chair Lewis noted when 
the city established the West End Farm Trail it brought a lot more people out there. Vice-Chair Lewis 
stated the trail was adopted before the new trail criteria that was established in 2019. Vice-Chair 
Lewis noted the there has been discussion on mitigation with fencing, landscaping, signage and 
possible changes to parking access. Vice-Chair Lewis does not feel the city should bear the cost for 
the mitigation and not sure what the answer is to reduce impact. Vice-Chair Lewis does not feel they 
can make a decision today. Vice-Chair Lewis noted the shooting is a concern and there are other 
people out there shooting.   
  
Ms. O’Brien presented pictures from a visit to the site to the Commission.  
 
Chair Tardiff noted there is no option to move the trail due to wetlands.  
 
Alternate Member Owers suggested for mitigation to build a fence and to have a more concrete plan.   
 
Member Lesser asked if there can be a motion to keep the trail open with an addendum to discuss 
mitigation at the next meeting.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated it can be on the agenda for next month.  
 
Ms. O’Brien asked if they are inviting the Marro’s back to discuss at the next meeting. 
 
Chair Tardiff stated they can invite them back to discuss at the next meeting. Chair Tardiff suggested 
there be a motion tonight on the question to discontinue or not. Then continue discussion about 
mitigation next month. Chair Tardiff is in favor of keeping this segment intact.  
 
Member Lesser moved, Member Coen seconded, to maintain the West End Farm Trail open and 
continue the discussion for mitigation next month and to engage with the Marro’s.  
 
Discussion
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
5 
 
Vice-Chair Lewis suggested to maybe start the conversation this evening because they maybe want 
staff to look into an item before next month. Vice-Chair Lewis suggested it not say they will start next 
month and make a condition on an effort to find mitigation with the Marro’s. 
 
Alternate Member Owers suggested to have staff input, forester impute on what works and does not 
work.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis stated if they are talking about a fence where will they be located and asked for 
information before the next meeting.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated that is not on the agenda for the public notice and there not be discussion.  
 
Ms. O’Brien stated they are starting on the conversation and not making a decision on the mitigation. 
They are inviting the Marro’s to discuss mitigation and at the past meeting there was discussion on 
installing a fence. Ms. O’Brien advised the Commission they need to keep in mind about the Bow 
Pioneers for the mitigation discussion.  
 
Chair Tardiff suggested to get all parties involved to go and do a site walk for a mitigation discussion.  
 
Member Chormann asked to change the wording in the motion to say potential mitigation. 
 
Member Lesser stated that is fair. Member Lesser moved, Member Coen seconded, to maintain the 
West End Farm Trail open and continue the discussion for potential mitigation next month and to 
engage with the Marro’s. All in favor. Member Porter abstained. The motion passed.  
  
Chair Tardiff asked for information for discussion on mitigation for next month.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis noted there are some areas where you can see into their backyard and suggested a 
fence. Vice-Chair Lewis noted at the parking lot they could install a fence. Vice-Chair Lewis 
suggested a fence right down the trail and there might need to be trees removed that could cost more 
money.  
 
Ms. O’Brien stated staff can look into a fence and will work with city surveyor and forester to see 
location for a fence or vegetative buffer. Ms. O’Brien suggested logs to delineate the trail and clear 
signage. Ms. O’Brien stated for the parking lot to open the front so it is more visible to deter from the 
activities receiving complaints.  
 
Mr. Bass stated staff does not know all of the questions. Mr. Bass stated it might be a better idea and 
then push to a date certain to follow leads.  
 
Member Coen stated it sounds like the Commission is making all of the concessions and not 
comfortable to say the Commission comes up with all of these things.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated that will be the future discussion to look at who bears what cost and that is open 
for a discussion.
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
6 
 
Alternate Member Owers stated he is not opposed to have the city contribute for the mitigate. 
However, there needs to be a good faith effort on their part that the signs come down, the cameras 
come down, the speakers come off and the hostility goes down. There needs to be good faith in a 
response to what the Commission is doing and be a good neighbor.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis agrees and there needs to be a conversation with the Marro’s’.  
 
Member Lesser has a concern about the photos that were shown at the public hearing there were 
children and other things that made her uncomfortable that they are taking photographs and showing 
them publicly of people on city property.   
 
Chair Tardiff suggested when looking at fencing to get an idea of the location of the shooting range. 
Chair Tardiff brought a concern for wire fencing because of wildlife.  
 
Member Chormann noted there is a buffer between the trail and the lawn. There could be a living 
hedge with wire fencing. If you install a fence there could be maintenance and costly. 
 
Ms. O’Brien asked if the Commission is asking staff come back with fencing options and cost for the 
next meeting along with vegetative buffer option.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis asked for realistic options.  
 
Member Lesser asked for feasibility on options.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis asked if the snow mobiles have rights on the trail and if the Commission can 
restrict the hours of the trail.  
 
Chair Tardiff asked for a formal site walk to be scheduled with all parties. 
 
4. Public Hearing regarding the donation of land located off of Stickney Hill at Tax Map and Lot 85/z 48 
a. Maps 
Ms. O’Brien stated the title search was completed and moving forward with the public hearing 
for the land donation. Ms. O’Brien noted the land is in the conservation area. The Commission 
can decide if want to take this land donation on. Once a decision is made and approved it will 
then be forwarded to City Council with the Commission’s recommendation.  
 
Alternate Member Owers asked if this is a 100% land donation.  
 
Ms. O’Brien replied from her understanding yes.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated the Swartz family reached out to the Commission previously a year or so 
ago about if there was interest in purchasing the property. Chair Tardiff stated they did not 
move forward and noted it is a nice property.  
 
Chair Tardiff opened the public hearing for public testimony and after no public testimony,
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
7 
 
Chair Tardiff closed the public hearing. 
 
Vice-Chair Lewis does not have an issue taking on this land donation and it is adjacent to a 
property the city already owns.  
  
Chair Tardiff noted it is not in a designated conservation area in the open space plan.  
 
Member Chormann moved, Member Coen seconded, to accept the land donation with gratitude. 
All in favor. The motion passed. 
 
5. New Business 
a. Planning Board CUP (2026-091)- 7 Rectory Rd 
Jessica Jacobson is present to represent this application. Ms. Jacobson pointed out the 
location of disturbance to the wetland buffer for the treatment and pretreat for state and city 
regulations. There are limited with site grading and topography of the area. The drainage is 
sheet flow impact to the pond. It is a bioretention pond based on existing site conditions, 
site topography and soil conditions. They need pretreatment with a sediment four bay. 
There is a segment four bay is why need impact to the wetland buffer. The disturbance is 
258 square feet. The previous impact had a larger impact. They were able to lessen the 
impact. It is supporting the parking for the campus for a lower proposed building.  
 
Chair Tardiff asked if the longer parking lot is being moved.  
 
Ms. Jacobson replied yes, there is an existing parking lot and they are reconfiguring it for 
the viewing for the field and placing the building and reorientation the parking.  
 
Chair Tardiff asked the area where the big parking lot is being moved and some of it is 
compacted.  
 
Ms. Jacobson replied yes, they are trying to limit the disturbance.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis stated it is straight forward and minimum impact. 
 
Vice-Chair Lewis moved, Member Porter seconded, to recommend the Planning Board approve 
the conditional use permit as submitted and the Commission has no concerns. All in favor. The 
motion passed. 
 
6. Reports 
a. Tree Subcommittee update – Rick Chormann 
Member Chormann asked if anyone attended the Ethan Tapper event over the weekend.   
 
Member Porter attended and thought it was a great event.  
 
b. City Open Space and Easements
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
8 
 
There was no discussion on this agenda item.  
 
c. City Council/Planning Board 
There was no discussion on this agenda item.  
 
7. Old Business 
a. Progress Report (Richards Forest Trail, West End Farm Trail, 16-foot easement trail follow-up 
discussion) Status of each, any outstanding items remaining to be done for the ones that are 
completed, permit status, installation of signage, etc. 
There was no discussion on this agenda item.  
 
b. Joint meetings with surrounding Conservation Commissions 
Ms. O’Brien stated there was a discussion with Chair Tardiff, Alternate Member Currie and Member 
Lesser about the baiting discussion. There was discussion to have a conversation with other towns to 
discuss baiting. On January 8th there will be a meeting with Bow and Boscawen to discuss bear 
baiting.     
 
Chair Tardiff stated this is a follow up to the request by Dan William request for bear baiting on city 
land. Chair Tardiff noted the state has a policy to apply for a permit in an area to bear bait. The state 
has staff to check sites with the bear baiting making sure they are using the site as intended. Chair 
Tardiff noted there is discussion on a federal level on bear baiting and not continuing due to impact to 
wildlife.   
 
Member Lesser stated it is a complicated issue. 
 
Chair Tardiff stated they started with researched gathering and brought back to Commission for a 
discussion or recommendation. If there was a policy they would open for public comment. There are 
a couple communities that have adopted policies.  
 
Ms. O’Brien suggested to have a discussion with the abutting towns if the Commission was to create 
a policy.   
 
Vice-Chair Lewis suggested to have a motion to nominate the three people (Tardiff, Currie and 
Lesser) will attend the January 8th meeting.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated there does not need to be a formal motion.  
 
8. Staff updates on items  
Ms. O’Brien stated the forest management plan has been received and there was a meeting with city staff 
with Mr. Klemarczyk. Mr. Klemarczyk gave a broad overview of the management plan. There will need 
to be a subcommittee established.
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
November 10, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
9 
 
Chair Tardiff stated Member Porter has already volunteered.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis nominated Member Chormann.  
 
Chair Tardiff and Vice-Chair Lewis also offered to volunteer to assist the subcommittee.  
 
Ms. O’Brien spoke with the city solicitor and staff is not breaching the RSA and updating the forest 
management plan and the draft will go through at an administrative level. The Conservation Commission 
will be able to see the forest management plan. Ms. O’Brien noted the meeting will be scheduled for the 
subgroup in January.    
 
Chair Tardiff asked if the meeting will be with staff.  
 
Ms. O’Brien stated does not know at this time and will be discussed at the next meeting with staff on how 
to proceed.  
 
Jeff Lewis left the meeting at 8:52 p.m. 
 
9. Non-Public RSA 91-A:3 II (d) 
On a motion made by Member Chormann, seconded by Member Porter, the Conservation 
Commission voted to enter the non-public session at 8:53 p.m. by roll call vote 5 in favor (Chormann,

On a motion made by Member Coen, seconded by Member Chormann, the Conservation Commission 
voted to exit the non-public session at 9:16 p.m. by roll call vote 5 in favor (Chormann, Coen, Lesser, 
Porter and Tardiff to 0 opposed. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
 
On a motion made by Member Coen, seconded by Member Chormann, the Conservation Commission 
made a motion at 9:17 p.m. to seal the non-public meeting minutes due to Render the proposed action 
ineffective; or by roll call vote 5 in favor (Chormann, Coen, Lesser, Porter and Tardiff) to 0 opposed. 
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
10. Adjourn 
 
Adjournment 
Member Chormann moved, seconded by Member Coen, to adjourn the meeting at 9:17 p.m. All in favor. 
Motion passed unanimously.
